documents.unit: Office of the Dean of Students, Honor Code
documents.title: Understanding Generative AI at UNCW
documents.summary: A student-facing section of the Honor Code resources page. It sets no university-wide rule on AI and says instructors have wide discretion, so students must follow each course's expectations. It adds five general tips: follow the syllabus, use AI to support thinking, use output responsibly, disclose and cite AI help, and keep personal data out of AI tools.
documents.stance_why: The page says "Instructors at UNCW have wide discretion in how they may incorporate AI into their course, if at all" and tells students to follow "the AI guidelines outlined in your syllabus". It bans nothing and requires nothing at university level beyond general tips, so the decision is handed to instructors.

units.why: Defines what the page means by generative AI, which sets the scope of the guidance: "tools that can create or significantly revise academic work". Definition, so informs; P61 fits because it defines the AI the policy covers.
units.anchor: tools that can create or significantly revise academic work

units.why: States a benefit and a condition: tools "can be helpful" and can "significantly aid students", but must be "used appropriately". It names benefits without making a rule, which matches P87 better than a stance type.
units.anchor: While AI tools can significantly aid students in various aspects of their learning journey
units.frag_end: they also must be used appropriately.

units.why: Says "their effectiveness depends on your understanding of both the tool and the subject", a caution that AI value depends on the user knowing the subject. It does not state a rule about verification or novices; the nearest fit is P42 (novices cannot judge AI output), but this is only a general caution.
units.anchor: their effectiveness depends on your understanding of both the tool and the subject
units.fit_note: Page says effectiveness depends on understanding the tool and subject; it does not mention beginners or foundational courses.

units.why: "It is the responsibility of students to communicate with their instructors about expectations regarding AI use in each course." This puts the duty on students to find out each course's rules, which is P78 (students learn and follow each course's rules), not P10, which is only about asking when unsure.
units.anchor: responsibility of students to communicate with their instructors about expectations regarding AI use

units.why: "Instructors at UNCW have wide discretion in how they may incorporate AI into their course, if at all." The university leaves whether AI is allowed to each instructor, which is P04.
units.anchor: have wide discretion in how they may incorporate AI into their course, if at all.
units.frag_end: into their course, if at all.

units.why: "Students must be certain that they are following their instructor’s expectations for the use of AI" binds students to comply with whatever the instructor sets. Chosen P78 over P29 because it concerns following course rules, not owning submitted work.
units.anchor: Students must be certain that they are following their instructor
units.policy: Students must be certain that they are following their instructor's expectations for the use of AI in their respective courses.

units.why: Tip 1: "Follow the AI guidelines outlined in your syllabus." Tells students the syllabus is where the rules are found and must be followed; this is P78 (find out and follow each course's rules).
units.anchor: Follow the AI guidelines outlined in your syllabus.

units.why: "These can potentially be different for each individual course you are enrolled in." States that one course's AI rules may differ from another's, so rules do not carry over; P11.
units.anchor: These can potentially be different for each individual course you are enrolled in.

units.why: "If you're unsure about what's allowed, ask your instructor." Direct instruction to ask when unsure; P10.
units.anchor: If you're unsure about what's allowed, ask your instructor.

units.why: Tip 2 says "AI tools are great for inspiring ideas, exploring topics, and examining problems". It welcomes AI for idea generation and exploration, so P15 with unit stance permit.
units.anchor: AI tools are great for inspiring ideas, exploring topics, and examining problems.
units.fit_note: Also mentions exploring topics and examining problems, which is wider than brainstorming alone.

units.why: "they should be used to support your thinking, not replace it": the student must stay the thinker and AI must not replace thinking. That is P32.
units.anchor: they should be used to support your thinking, not replace it.

units.why: "Make sure your work reflects your own understanding." Requires submitted work to reflect the student's own understanding. P30 (understand what you submit) fits better than P29 because the focus is understanding, not ownership.
units.anchor: Make sure your work reflects your own understanding.
units.fit_note: Says work must reflect own understanding; does not say explain every line.

units.why: Tip 3: "Use AI generated content in a responsible way." A general call to responsible use with no specific content, so P116.
units.anchor: Use AI generated content in a responsible way.

units.why: "AI generated outputs are known to potentially have biases, inaccuracies, and can elicit ethical concerns." Warns outputs may be wrong or biased, which is P31; it does not explicitly tell students to verify, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: AI generated outputs are known to potentially have biases, inaccuracies, and can elicit ethical concerns.
units.fit_note: States that output can be biased or inaccurate and raise ethical concerns; no instruction to verify.

units.why: Tip 4: "Be transparent and open about how you are using AI generated content. Properly document its use as necessary." Students must be open about and document AI use, so P24.
units.anchor: Be transparent and open about how you are using AI generated content.

units.why: "You are expected to disclose, explain, and cite any AI assistance in your work, following relevant standards (e.g., APA, MLA, or course guidelines)." Sets an expectation to disclose, explain and cite any AI help; P24. It does not require tool, prompt and output details, so not P25.
units.anchor: You are expected to disclose, explain, and cite any AI assistance in your work

units.why: Tip 5: "Never input personal or confidential information into generative AI tools." A flat ban on entering personal or confidential data; P50 protects personal data.
units.anchor: Never input personal or confidential information into generative AI tools.

units.why: Gives the reason for the data rule: "there's always a risk of data breaches or unauthorized access" even with encryption. Rationale for privacy, so informs under P50.
units.anchor: there's always a risk of data breaches or unauthorized access

units.why: "please check out the AI Hub" for "the latest information" about AI at UNCW. Directs readers to another page for current guidance, which is P115.
units.anchor: For the latest information about what’s happening at UNCW regarding AI please check out the
units.frag_end: please check out the AI Hub.

units.why: The resource list sends students to the Writing Center, Writing Lab, Math Services, Supplemental Instruction and tutoring: "free tutoring services in most University Studies courses". Directs students to human help, P72, although it is not specific to AI.
units.anchor: free tutoring services in most University Studies courses and select non-University Studies Courses
units.fit_note: Lists human support services for academic struggles; none are tied to AI use.

notes: Only one document (university layer). No school, computing or course documents were included. The page gives no enforcement, penalty or exam rules for AI.
